clue.text: Greek facility producing oil

parts.note: facility in the sense of ease or effortlessness

explanation.surface: A Greek plant is turning out olive oil.
explanation.definitionFit: To grease a hinge is to oil it; both mean lubricate.

clue.text: Giant dog decapitated aggressive person

parts.note: Gog is a legendary giant, as in Gog and Magog

indicators.note: decapitated means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A giant dog loses its head to a fierce attacker.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-getter is a pushy, ambitious person, aggressive in pursuit of success.

clue.text: Woman whos welcome to come up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, a welcome

explanation.surface: A woman who has a warm greeting for visitors coming upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Girl missing LA in southern Swiss city

indicators.note: missing means the named letters are left out

parts.note: Lausanne is a city in western Switzerland

explanation.surface: A girl who misses Los Angeles finds herself in a Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'LA' looks like Los Angeles, but it is just the letters dropped from LAUSANNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Susanne is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Stability cut by 40% after withdrawing American hero

indicators.note: after places the shortened word behind the turned piece
withdrawing means drawing back, so the short word for American is turned round
a ten-letter word cut by forty per cent loses four letters, here its tail

parts.note: stability is permanence

explanation.surface: A financial report: stability slashed by forty per cent after American investors pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' turns US into SU; 'cut by 40%' keeps the first six of PERMANENCE's ten letters, PERMAN. The held clue was garbled, so the scan's wording is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book Man of Steel is the archetypal superhero, so a hero describes him.

clue.text: Below par. I'm duly developing so?

definitions.text: Below par. I'm duly developing so?

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone below par but steadily improving describes their own progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges BELOW PAR I'M DULY; someone rising from below par fits the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Upwardly mobile describes someone rising in social or economic status.

clue.text: Source of peace when inserted in hearing organs

definitions.text: Source of peace when inserted in hearing organs

indicators.note: inserted in means placed inside the pair of words

parts.note: an ear is a hearing organ
lug is British slang for an ear

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Something that brings quiet once put in your ears.
explanation.walkthrough: Lug is British slang for an ear, and 'when inserted in' puts P inside. The whole clue also describes the answer, so it reads both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug pushed into the ear blocks noise and brings peace and quiet.

clue.text: Fail to see what's right, accepting deception?

definitions.text: Fail to see what's right, accepting deception?

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the pair holds the word for deception

parts.note: to miss something is to fail to see it
a con is a deception or trick
true means correct, right

explanation.surface: Someone who misses the truth because they have swallowed a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS + TRUE takes in CON, giving MIS-CON-S-TRUE. The held clue was garbled, so the scan's wording is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To misconstrue is to misinterpret, failing to see the right meaning.

clue.text: Case for treatment in cattle, laid up, almost

indicators.note: in means the casing letters go inside the reversed word
in a down clue laid up means set upwards, read backwards

parts.note: oxen are cattle

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A vet's note on treating cattle that are laid up, nearly recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: OXEN read upwards gives NEXO, which takes TT, the first and last letters of 'treatment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Next to can mean nearly, as in next to impossible.

clue.text: Lesson I describe as a means of preserving old language

parts.note: a class is a lesson
to call something a name is to describe it as such
a tin preserves food

explanation.surface: A teacher calls their lesson a way of keeping a dead language alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical Latin is the literary language of ancient Rome, an old tongue.

clue.text: Who could shape large bowls containing silicates primarily?

definitions.text: Who could shape large bowls containing silicates primarily?

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged words hold the extra letter inside
to shape something is to rework it, so the letters of the two words are rearranged
primarily picks the first letter of the word silicates

explanation.surface: A riddle asking who might form big bowls from silicate-based material.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of LARGE BOWLS (signalled by 'could shape') holds S, the first letter of 'silicates'; the whole clue also describes the craftsman, since glass is made from silicates.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who blows molten glass into vessels such as bowls fits the riddle exactly.

clue.text: This clue number's opposite number?

indicators.note: opposite here means facing the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: this is clue 11, XI in Roman numerals, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A question about which number sits opposite this one, as on a die or a clock face.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is numbered 11, so 'This clue number's' is XI'S; 'opposite' reads XIS backwards. The surface tempts you to look for the number facing 11 on a dial.
explanation.definitionFit: Six is simply a number, a plain example of the category named.

clue.text: Following temperature, star worried about infection

indicators.note: following temperature means the other pieces come after its abbreviation
about means turned around, so the two words joined are read backwards

parts.note: the sun is a star
ate in the sense of worried at, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: After a high temperature, a celebrity frets about catching something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses both words together, giving ETANUS; 'worried' in the sense of 'ate at' is the less obvious synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus, or lockjaw, is a bacterial infection usually caught through wounds.

clue.text: A German I twice introduced to dotty aunt, making meditative movements

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside the rearranged word
dotty means crazy, so the letters are mixed up
twice means the piece appears two times

parts.note: ich is German for I

explanation.surface: A German pair meet an eccentric aunt who does slow exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dotty' rearranges the aunt around the insertion; tai chi chuan is the full name of the exercise usually shortened to tai chi.
explanation.definitionFit: Tai chi chuan is a Chinese martial art practised as slow, meditative exercise.

clue.text: Circle line left in shambles for launch of new stock

indicators.note: in means the three short pieces go inside the word for shambles

parts.note: a rout is a disorderly retreat, a shambles
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: London's Circle line is left in chaos when new trains are introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle line' looks like the London Underground route, but it is O and L separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollout is the introduction of a new product or service to the market.

clue.text: Might one provide breakdown of oldies' impetigo

definitions.text: Might one provide breakdown of oldies' impetigo

indicators.note: a breakdown of something splits it apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about who would analyse a skin infection among old people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakdown of' rearranges OLDIES IMPETIGO; the whole clue describes a scientist who analyses the spread of disease.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemiologist studies how diseases such as impetigo are distributed in a population.

clue.text: Tsar up in rages because of him?

definitions.text: Tsar up in rages because of him?

indicators.note: rages suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A Russian tsar flies into a fury because of one man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is fodder: 'rages' rearranges TSAR UP IN. The Romanovs' mystic adviser famously enraged court and country.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasputin was the mystic whose influence over the last tsar's family caused uproar.

clue.text: Shot king instead of knight in Australian state after zealot mentioned dreamlike visions

indicators.note: after puts the state-based piece behind the spoken piece
mentioned means spoken, so the word for zealot is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast or zealot

indicators.note: in means the word for shot goes inside the altered state name
instead of means one letter is swapped in for another

parts.note: Tasmania is an Australian island state
N is the chess notation for knight
R is short for Latin rex, king
a shot is a go, an attempt

explanation.surface: A grim scene: a king is shot in place of a knight in Tasmania by a fanatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' makes FAN sound as PHAN; 'instead of' swaps knight for king, giving TASMARIA, and 'in' puts the shot inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantasmagoria is a shifting series of illusory or dreamlike images.

clue.text: Criticise arrest involving tip off

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round the rearranged piece

parts.note: nick is British slang for arrest

indicators.note: off means awry or wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Police make an arrest after a tip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip off' looks like an informant's message, but 'off' jumbles the three letters, giving TPI, which 'involving' wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to criticise fussily over trivial details.

clue.text: Allow area round island's rough ice

indicators.note: round means surrounding the letter for island

parts.note: to grant is to allow
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Allowing an area around an island for rough sea ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A granita is a coarse-textured Italian water ice, roughly crystalline.

clue.text: With a change of hands, grab fork

indicators.note: hands here are left and right, so the L becomes an R

parts.note: to clutch is to grab

explanation.surface: Changing hands, someone grabs a garden fork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of hands' looks like passing an object along, but it means swapping left for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A crutch is a forked support, and also the fork of the body or a tree.

clue.text: Grid losing core resistance set back performance

indicators.note: set back means the assembled letters are turned round
the core of a word is its middle letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a lattice is a grid of crossing strips
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An electrical grid failure delays a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: LATTICE loses its middle T ('losing core') to give LATICE; with R added, 'set back' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance, often by a soloist.

clue.text: Backsliding boozer's about to idle — and get fired?

indicators.note: about means the reversed word wraps round the word for idle
backsliding means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub; the 's stands for has
to laze is to idle

explanation.surface: A relapsing drinker is going to slack off at work and risk the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backsliding' turns PUB into BUP, which goes 'about' LAZE. 'get fired' looks like losing a job but means catch fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaze up is to burst into flame, to catch fire suddenly.

clue.text: Character having no slack cut

indicators.note: cut means a letter is trimmed from the end

parts.note: a rope with no slack is taut

explanation.surface: A person with no spare flesh is cut, i.e. lean and muscular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims the last T. A character can be a letter of an alphabet, here Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a written character.

clue.text: Smart, impoverished count supplanting duke

indicators.note: supplanting means one piece takes the place of another

parts.note: indigent means poor, impoverished
to tell is to count, as with tellers counting votes

explanation.surface: A clever but poor count replaces a duke in some aristocratic intrigue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a nobleman next to 'duke', but it means TELL, as in counting.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and intelligent both describe someone quick-witted and clever.

clue.text: Result of nurse ignoring onset?

indicators.note: ignoring the onset means dropping the first letter

parts.note: to tend is to nurse

explanation.surface: What happens when a nurse ignores the onset of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is an outcome or result, as in to that end.

clue.text: Old colony making central switch to sound of horn and gong

indicators.note: central switch means the two middle letters trade places

parts.note: a horn honks
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former colony changes its tune to horns and gongs.
explanation.walkthrough: HONK + GONG gives HONKGONG; switching the central K and G gives the answer. Hong Kong was a British colony until 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: The territory was a British colony until its handover to China in 1997.

clue.text: Head off provocation over new plot?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters run backwards
head off removes the first letter

parts.note: a red rag (to a bull) is a provocation

explanation.surface: Heading off a provocation over a new scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: RED RAG loses its head R, and 'over' reverses EDRAG to GARDE. The question mark admits a plot here is of land, not a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is a plot of land for growing plants.
